summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Anton K. v. State, Department of Family & Community Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: ICWA's active-efforts duty continues even while a parent is incarcerated — incarceration affects only what efforts are possible — and the court affirmed termination after finding OCS's efforts, viewed in their entirety, were active.
key_cases.relevance: Preserves the reunification obligation even when permanency timelines press against it.
key_cases.quote: ICWA also does not contain any provision allowing a court to approve the discontinuation of active efforts.

key_cases.case_name: Mona J. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: The superior court erred in stating that active efforts depend on a parent's willingness to engage, because the active-efforts inquiry focuses primarily on what OCS did, though the court declined to overturn precedent allowing consideration of parental non-cooperation and futility.
key_cases.relevance: Preserves the reunification duty as an agency obligation rather than a conditional offer.
key_cases.quote: the active efforts inquiry depends primarily on OCS's efforts, not the parent's reaction to those efforts

key_cases.case_name: Ronald H. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Termination of a father's rights to his Indian children, adjudicated in need of aid because of his domestic violence and aggressive behavior, was affirmed because the superior court did not err in finding OCS made active efforts.
key_cases.relevance: Measures whether reunification services were adequate before permanency shifted away from the parent.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the superior court did not err in finding that active efforts were made and affirm the termination order.

key_cases.case_name: Simone H. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: The trial court acted within its discretion in refusing to release the child's therapy records to the mother for use at the termination trial, and substantial evidence supported the finding that OCS made reasonable efforts to reunify the family.
key_cases.relevance: Confirms reasonable efforts to reunify were made before reunification was abandoned.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the trial court acted within its discretion in denying Simone's request for access to Irving's therapy records

extended_foster_care_age: To the 21st birthday by court order only: state custody ends at the 19th birthday unless the court grants one-year extensions past 19, which require the person's consent and a best-interests finding, and a person already released from care may ask the court to resume custody before the 21st birthday (Alaska Stat. § 47.10.080(c)(1)(B), § 47.10.080(v), § 47.10.100(a))
